title.en: World Desk
title.zh: 全球焦点

strap.en: A fast view of global affairs, conflict, diplomacy, and human need.
strap.zh: 快速掌握国际局势、冲突、外交与人类处境。

title.en: US is ‘simply choosing not to stop’ Ebola outbreak after massive public health cuts, experts say
title.zh: 美国专家称，大规模公共卫生削减后，美国“就是选择不阻止”埃博拉疫情

summary.en: Experts report hundreds of Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo, noting that the US appears to be doing little to help stop the outbreak after significant cuts to global public health initiatives and scientific research.
summary.zh: 专家报告称，刚果民主共和国已出现数百例埃博拉病例，并指出在美国大幅削减全球公共卫生项目和科学研究后，美国似乎没有采取多少措施来阻止疫情蔓延。

body.en: Hundreds of cases reported in the DRC after USAID has been dismantled and key scientific research canceled A previously undetected outbreak of Ebola is coursing through parts of central Africa, and the US appears to be doing little to help stop it, after massive cuts to global and domestic public health efforts. There is no cure and no vaccine for the rare Bundibugyo variant of Ebola, which has caused two outbreaks in recent decades. Health leaders and scientists are now racing to understand where the virus is spreading and attempting to stop it – but the US is notably absent in these efforts. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国国际开发署被解散、关键科学研究被取消后，刚果民主共和国报告了数百起病例。此前未被发现的埃博拉疫情正在中非部分地区蔓延，在大规模削减全球和国内公共卫生工作后，美国似乎没有采取任何措施来帮助阻止疫情。罕见的本迪布焦变种埃博拉病毒目前尚无治愈方法，也没有疫苗，该病毒近几十年来已引发两次疫情。卫生领导人和科学家现在正在竞相了解病毒在哪里传播并试图阻止它，但美国在这些努力中明显缺席。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights the profound responsibility of nations to act justly and compassionately, especially in global health crises. When public health initiatives are cut and outbreaks are left unchecked, it is a failure to "do what is right and just" for the vulnerable. Our shared humanity calls us to support efforts that protect all people from suffering.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了各国在应对全球健康危机时，秉持公义和怜悯的重大责任。当公共卫生项目被削减，疫情蔓延得不到遏制时，这便是未能为弱势群体“行公义、施公平”。我们共同的人性呼唤我们支持保护所有人免受苦难的努力。

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Bernie Sanders backs climate activist in close Michigan congressional primary
title.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯支持密歇根州国会初选中的气候活动家

summary.en: Bernie Sanders has endorsed Will Lawrence, a climate activist and outspoken opponent of AI data centers, in a tight Michigan congressional primary. Lawrence is advocating for a nationwide moratorium on data centers, citing environmental concerns as three mega-complexes are planned for the swing district.
summary.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯在密歇根州一场激烈的国会初选中，支持了气候活动家威尔·劳伦斯，劳伦斯是人工智能数据中心的坚定反对者。该摇摆选区计划建设三个大型数据中心，劳伦斯呼吁全国暂停数据中心建设，理由是环境问题。

body.en: Will Lawrence, an outspoken opponent of AI data centers, is running in swing district where three mega complexes loom A prominent environmental organizer calling for a nationwide moratorium on data centers as he runs for the Democratic nomination in a swing Michigan congressional district has secured an endorsement from Bernie Sanders. Will Lawrence, co-founder of the youth-led Sunrise Movement climate justice group, was a key figure behind the campaign for a Green New Deal to battle economic and racial injustice while also fighting climate change. Continue reading...
body.zh: 直言不讳地反对人工智能数据中心的威尔·劳伦斯(Will Lawrence)正在三座大型综合体隐现的摇摆选区竞选。一位著名的环保组织者在密歇根州摇摆国会选区竞选民主党提名时呼吁在全国范围内暂停数据中心建设，该组织已获得伯尼·桑德斯(Bernie Sanders)的支持。威尔·劳伦斯是青年领导的日出运动气候正义组织的联合创始人，他是绿色新政运动背后的关键人物，该运动旨在对抗经济和种族不平等，同时应对气候变化。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for a moratorium on AI data centers highlights our ongoing responsibility to care for the earth. Just as humanity was placed in the Garden to tend and keep it, we are entrusted with stewarding creation wisely. This includes carefully considering the environmental impact of new technologies and developments.
reflection.zh: 呼吁暂停人工智能数据中心建设，凸显了我们持续照管地球的责任。正如人类被安置在伊甸园中看守和管理它一样，我们也受托智慧地管理受造物。这包括仔细考量新技术和新发展对环境的影响。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: DR Congo cancels World Cup training camp over Ebola outbreak
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国因埃博拉疫情取消世界杯训练营

summary.en: An Ebola outbreak, caused by a rare species, has led to the cancellation of a World Cup training camp in DR Congo. The disease is reported to have caused 139 deaths so far.
summary.zh: 刚果民主共和国因一种罕见的埃博拉病毒爆发而取消了世界杯训练营。据报道，此次疫情已导致139人死亡。

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has cancelled its pre-World Cup training camp in the capital, Kinshasa, because of an Ebola outbreak in the east of the country.

Preparations have been moved to Belgium amid the upsurge, which is thought to have killed more than 130 people.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has called the outbreak a "public health emergency of international concern", but said it was not at pandemic level.

Jerry Kalemo, a spokesperson for the national football team, told international media that pre-tournament games in Europe would go ahead as planned, as the squad gears up for their first World Cup since 1974.

DR Congo are due to play friendly matches against Denmark, on 3 June in Belgium, and Chile, on 9 June in Spain, ahead of the World Cup finals.

A spokesperson for the DR Congo team told the Reuters news agency that the squad's training camp had been cancelled due to travel restrictions imposed by the US, who are hosting the World Cup this summer, along with Mexico and Canada.

The US' public health agency has banned entry from non-Americans who have been in the DR Congo, Uganda or South Sudan in the previous 21 days, in response to the Ebola outbreak.

All DR Congo's players, as well as the team's French coach, Sébastien Desabre, are based outside the central African country and will therefore not be affected by the restrictions now the training camp has been cancelled.

The high-profile event in Kinshasa was supposed to have been attended by fans, along with DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi, according to Reuters.

Kinshasa is roughly 1,800 km (1,120m) away from the eastern Ituri province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak. There have not yet been any reported cases in the city.

On Wednesday, the WHO said 139 people were thought to have died, out of 600 suspected cases. However, on the same day, Congolese health minister Samuel Roger Kamba told state broadcaster RTNC TV that authorities had registered 159 deaths.

The outbreak has been caused by a rare species of Ebola known as Bundibugyo. There is currently no vaccine for this species and the WHO has said it could take up to nine months for a jab to be ready .
body.zh: 由于该国东部爆发埃博拉疫情，刚果民主共和国取消了在首都金沙萨举行的世界杯前训练营。 抗议活动已造成 130 多人死亡，准备工作已转移至比利时。 世界卫生组织（WHO）称此次疫情为“国际关注的突发公共卫生事件”，但表示尚未达到大流行的程度。 国家足球队发言人杰里·卡莱莫告诉国际媒体，欧洲赛前比赛将按计划进行，球队正在为自 1974 年以来的首次世界杯做准备。 在世界杯决赛之前，刚果民主共和国将于 6 月 3 日在比利时与丹麦进行友谊赛，并于 6 月 9 日在西班牙与智利进行友谊赛。 刚果民主共和国队的发言人告诉路透社，由于今年夏天主办世界杯的美国、墨西哥和加拿大实施旅行限制，该队的训练营已被取消。 为了应对埃博拉疫情，美国公共卫生机构已禁止过去 21 天内去过刚果民主共和国、乌干达或南苏丹的非美国人入境。 刚果民主共和国的所有球员以及球队的法国教练塞巴斯蒂安·德萨布雷都居住在刚果民主共和国以外的国家，因此不会受到训练营取消后的限制的影响。 据路透社报道，这场在金沙萨举行的备受瞩目的活动原本应该有球迷参加，包括刚果民主共和国总统菲利克斯·齐塞克迪。 金沙萨距埃博拉疫情中心东部伊图里省约 1,800 公里（1,120m）。该市尚未报告任何病例。 周三，世界卫生组织表示，600 例疑似病例中，有 139 人被认为死亡。然而，同一天，刚果卫生部长塞缪尔·罗杰·坎巴 (Samuel Roger Kamba) 告诉国家广播公司 RTNC TV，当局已登记 159 人死亡。 此次疫情是由一种名为本迪布焦（Bundibugyo）的稀有埃博拉病毒引起的。目前还没有针对该物种的疫苗，世界卫生组织表示，可能需要长达九个月的时间才能准备好疫苗。

reflection.en: The news of an Ebola outbreak and its tragic toll reminds us of life's fragility and the pervasive presence of illness in our world. In such times, we are called to remember those afflicted and to lift them in prayer, trusting in God's compassion and healing power.
reflection.zh: 埃博拉疫情爆发及其悲惨的死亡人数提醒我们生命的脆弱，以及疾病在我们世界中普遍存在。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召记念那些受苦的人，并为他们祷告，信靠雅伟的怜悯和医治大能。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: Net migration into UK almost halved in 2025, official figures show – politics live
title.zh: 官方数据显示，2025年英国净移民人数几乎减半

summary.en: Official figures show that net migration into the UK almost halved in 2025, reaching 171,000, the lowest since 2021. The Home Office also reported that 20,885 asylum seekers were temporarily housed in hotels.
summary.zh: 官方数据显示，2025年英国净移民人数几乎减半，达到17.1万人，为2021年以来的最低水平。内政部还报告称，截至目前，有20,885名寻求庇护者暂时安置在酒店中。

body.en: Office for National Statistics says figure of 171,000 in year to December 2025 was the lowest since 2021 The Home Office has also published asylum figures this morning. These show that the number of asylum seekers being housed temporarily in hotels stood at 20,885 at the end of March 2026, down 35% year-on-year from 32,326. The Press Association says: It is the lowest figure since data was first reported in 2022, Home Office figures show. The total had climbed as high as 56,018 at the end of September 2023. Brits are leaving on a massive scale and non-EU immigration remains far too high. Mass immigration undermines our society and low wage immigration is bad for the economy. British families feel it in lower wages, longer waiting lists for public services and housing shortages. Labour must go further and reform indefinite leave to remain before their hard-left flank forces them to abandon it altogether. Continue reading...
body.zh: 英国国家统计局表示，截至 2025 年 12 月的这一数字为 171,000 人，是 2021 年以来的最低水平。内政部今天上午也公布了庇护数据。这些数据显示，截至2026年3月，临时安置在酒店的寻求庇护者人数为20,885人，比去年同期的32,326人减少了35%。新闻协会表示：内政部数据显示，这是自 2022 年首次报告数据以来的最低数字。截至 2023 年 9 月底，总数已攀升至 56,018 人。英国人正在大规模离开，非欧盟移民人数仍然过高。大规模移民破坏我们的社会，低工资移民不利于经济。英国家庭在工资较低、公共服务等候名单较长以及住房短缺等方面感受到了这一点。工党必须进一步改革无限期居留权，以免他们的极左翼迫使他们完全放弃这一政策。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As nations grapple with migration figures and policies, the underlying call remains to consider how we treat those who seek a new home among us. Leviticus 19:33-34 reminds us to welcome foreigners as if they were native-born, remembering our shared human experience. This principle encourages compassion and fair treatment for all who reside in our land.
reflection.zh: 当各国都在处理移民数据和政策时，其核心呼召仍然是思考我们如何对待那些在我们中间寻求新家园的人。利未记19:33-34提醒我们，雅伟神命令我们要像对待本地人一样欢迎寄居的外国人，并记住我们共同的人类经历。这一原则鼓励我们对所有居住在我们土地上的人抱有怜悯和公平的对待。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Nvidia's record result fails to impress investors
title.zh: 英伟达创纪录业绩未能打动投资者

summary.en: Chip giant Nvidia reported another quarter of strong financial results, but its shares declined after-hours as investors expressed concerns about the company's ability to sustain its rapid growth amidst increasing competition.
summary.zh: 芯片巨头英伟达公布了又一份亮眼的财务业绩，但其股价在盘后下跌，因为投资者质疑该公司在日益激烈的竞争中能否保持其增长速度。

body.en:
Chip giant Nvidia reported yet another record quarter with sales and profits beating expectations, seemingly suggesting there's no slowdown in sight for the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta, meaning its results are closely watched.

The company reported first-quarter revenue was up 85% on the year to $81.6bn (£60.7bn), while net income more than tripled to $58.3bn.

However, shares in the company fell 1.6% in after-hours trading with analysts saying investors have got used to Nvidia delivering stellar results and amid some concerns that the firm will face growing competition.

Nvidia is the world's most valuable company, with a stock market value of around $5.3 trillion.

In its latest results, it said sales were driven by strong growth in its data centre division.

It forecasts spending on AI infrastructure to be between $3tn and $4tn a year by the end of this decade.

"Demand has gone parabolic," chief executive Jensen Huang told analysts on a conference call. "The reason is simple: the era of agentic AI is here."

But its shares fell in extended trading, which Ruth Foxe-Blader, managing partner at US venture capital firm Citrine Venture Partners, put down to "a law of large numbers".

"Nvidia represents 8% of the S&P 500. Unless there's a belief in this continued parabolic growth it's difficult for investors to get super excited, although Nvidia posted outstanding numbers," she told the BBC.

"But it's just investors seeking that hypergrowth, which is indicating an early sell-off."

Victoria Scholar, head of investment at interactive investor, agreed that while it was a strong quarter for the company, "the bar is very high for the artificial intelligence bellwether which has made a habit out of delivering incredibly impressive results.

"Plus investors 'bought the rumour, sold the fact' as shares had already rallied ahead of earnings," she added.

"There are some concerns among Nvidia investors about the growing threat of competition as the data centre landscape shifts and hyperscalers develop their own chips."
body.zh: 芯片巨头英伟达公布了又一个创纪录的季度业绩，其销售额和利润都超出了预期，这似乎表明人工智能（AI）热潮不会放缓。 Nvidia 是人工智能基础设施领域的核心参与者，为 OpenAI 和 Meta 等领先的人工智能模型开发商提供芯片，这意味着其结果受到密切关注。 该公司公布第一季度营收同比增长 85%，达到 816 亿美元（607 亿英镑），净利润增长两倍多，达到 583 亿美元。 然而，该公司股价在盘后交易中下跌 1.6%，分析师表示，投资者已经习惯了 Nvidia 提供的出色业绩，并且有些人担心该公司将面临日益激烈的竞争。 Nvidia 是全球最有价值的公司，其股票市值约为 5.3 万亿美元。 该公司在最新业绩中表示，销售额是由数据中心部门的强劲增长推动的。 它预测到本十年末，每年人工智能基础设施的支出将在 3 万亿美元到 4 万亿美元之间。 首席执行官黄仁勋在电话会议上对分析师表示：“需求呈抛物线式增长。” “原因很简单：代理人工智能时代已经到来。” 但其股价在盘后交易中下跌，美国风险投资公司 Citrine Venture Partners 的管理合伙人露丝·福克斯-布拉德 (Ruth Foxe-Blader) 将其归因于“大数法则”。 “英伟达占标准普尔 500 指数的 8%。除非相信这种持续的抛物线增长，否则投资者很难感到超级兴奋，尽管英伟达公布了出色的数据，”她告诉 BBC。 “但这只是投资者寻求高速增长，这表明早期抛售。” Interactive Investor的投资主管Victoria Scholar同意，虽然该公司的季度表现强劲，但“对于人工智能领头羊来说，门槛非常高，它已经习惯于提供令人难以置信的令人印象深刻的业绩。 她补充道：“加上投资者‘买了谣言，卖出了事实’，因为股价在财报发布前就已经上涨。” “随着数据中心格局的变化和超大规模企业开发自己的芯片，英伟达投资者对日益增长的竞争威胁感到担忧。”

reflection.en: Even stellar business achievements can feel fleeting when the focus is solely on the next quarter's growth and market expectations. This reminds us that while striving for excellence is good, true and lasting value lies beyond the perishable crowns of worldly success. Our ultimate pursuit should be for that which endures eternally.
reflection.zh: 即使是卓越的商业成就，当焦点只放在下一季度的增长和市场预期时，也可能显得转瞬即逝。这提醒我们，虽然追求卓越是好的，但真正持久的价值超越了世俗成功那易朽的冠冕。我们最终的追求，应是那永恒不朽之事。

verse.textEn: Everyone who competes in the games goes into strict training. They do it to get a crown that will not last, but we do it to get a crown that will last forever.
verse.textZh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

title.en: Net migration to UK falls by nearly 50% after Labour’s vow to cut numbers
title.zh: 英国净移民人数下降近50%，此前工党曾誓言削减移民数量

summary.en: Official figures show that net migration to the UK fell by nearly 50% to 171,000 last year. This decline is seen as a significant development in a key political debate.
summary.zh: 官方数据显示，去年英国净移民人数下降近50%，至17.1万人。这一降幅被视为一场重要政治辩论中的关键进展。

body.en: Decline to 171,000 last year will encourage ministers in what is seen as a battleground issue against Reform UK politics live – latest updates Net migration to the UK fell by nearly 50% to 171,000 last year, according to official figures released on Thursday, in what will be seen as a boost for Keir Starmer’s government. Data released by the Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed the difference between the number of people moving to the UK and the number of people leaving was at its lowest level since 2021. Continue reading...
body.zh: 去年下降至 171,000 人，将鼓励部长们应对被视为反对英国政治改革的战场问题——最新动态 根据周四公布的官方数据，去年英国净移民人数下降近 50%，至 171,000 人，这将被视为对基尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 政府的推动。英国国家统计局（ONS）发布的数据显示，移居英国的人数与离开英国的人数之差处于2021年以来的最低水平。继续阅读...

reflection.en: National discussions about migration often become complex, balancing economic needs, social integration, and humanitarian concerns. Deuteronomy 10:19 reminds us of a foundational principle: to love and welcome the foreigner, remembering our own shared human experience of being strangers. This perspective encourages us to approach migration policies with...
reflection.zh: 关于移民的国家讨论往往复杂，需要平衡经济需求、社会融合和人道主义关切。申命记10:19提醒我们一个基本原则：要爱护寄居的，因为我们自己也曾是寄居的。这一视角鼓励我们在制定移民政策时，既要有智慧，也要有怜悯。

verse.textEn: And you are to love those who are foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: ‘Peace in Europe no longer default situation’, warns Czech president Petr Pavel – Europe live
title.zh: 捷克总统彼得·帕维尔警告：‘欧洲和平不再是默认状态’

summary.en: European state officials are meeting in Prague for a global security conference, where Czech President Petr Pavel warned that peace in Europe can no longer be taken for granted. This comes as a Russian foreign ministry spokesperson also made statements regarding Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
summary.zh: 欧洲各国官员正在布拉格举行全球安全会议，捷克总统彼得·帕维尔在会上警告称，欧洲的和平不再是理所当然的默认状态。与此同时，俄罗斯外交部发言人也对乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基发表了言论。

body.en: European state officials are meeting in Prague to discuss the state of the transatlantic alliance at a global security conference Just as Pavel was speaking in Prague, Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told reporters that Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy was pursuing escalation of the conflict between the two countries. It’s quite a claim given (checks notes) Russia’s continued and relentless invasion of Ukraine for years. “ Ukraine has demonstrated not only determination and heroism, but also unbelievable capacity to adjust, to innovate, to change. It is something that we in Europe have lost through many regulatory measures that are necessary in peacetime, but of course in conflict you have to be … flexible and achieve the results in shortest possible time. … Continue reading...
body.zh: 欧洲国家官员正在布拉格举行全球安全会议，讨论跨大西洋联盟的状况。就在帕维尔在布拉格发表讲话时，俄罗斯外交部发言人玛丽亚·扎哈罗娃告诉记者，乌克兰总统泽连斯基正在寻求升级两国之间的冲突。考虑到俄罗斯多年来对乌克兰持续无情的入侵，这是一个相当有说服力的说法（检查笔记）。 “乌克兰不仅表现出了决心和英雄主义，而且还表现出了令人难以置信的调整、创新和变革的能力。这是我们欧洲人通过和平时期必要的许多监管措施而失去的东西，但当然在冲突中你必须……灵活并在尽可能短的时间内取得成果。……继续阅读...

reflection.en: The warning that peace is no longer a default situation reminds us that harmony often requires intentional effort and vigilance. In a world of complex tensions, we are called to actively pursue peace wherever and whenever possible.
reflection.zh: 和平不再是默认状态的警告提醒我们，和谐常常需要刻意的努力和警惕。在一个充满复杂张力的世界里，我们蒙召在任何可能的情况下积极追求和平。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Far-right Israeli minister condemned for taunting handcuffed Gaza flotilla activists
title.zh: 极右翼以色列部长因嘲讽被戴手铐的加沙船队活动人士而受谴责

summary.en: France and Italy have condemned an Israeli minister for a video showing him taunting dozens of activists who were detained at an Israeli port.
summary.zh: 法国和意大利等国谴责了一段视频，视频中一名以色列部长嘲讽了在以色列港口被拘留的数十名活动人士。

body.en:
There has been international condemnation of Israel's treatment of pro-Palestinian activists who were on board a Gaza-bound aid flotilla intercepted by Israeli naval forces.

The US, the UK, France, Italy and Canada were among the countries which expressed outrage after far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir posted a video showing himself taunting activists kneeling with their hands tied behind their backs.

His actions also drew rare criticism from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who said they were "not in line with Israel's values".

A rights group representing the detainees said they had been physically abused, resulting in "severe, widespread injuries".

Adalah said at least three people had been taken to hospital and were later discharged.

"[Adalah's] lawyers documented dozens of participants with suspected broken ribs and resulting difficulty in breathing," it said.

"Reports also indicated the frequent use of Tasers against participants, as well as injuries sustained from the use of rubber bullets during the interception...

The group said activists were also "subjected to severe degradation and sexual harassment and humiliation".

More than 50 boats taking part in the Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF) set sail from Turkey last Thursday carrying a token amount of aid. Four hundred and thirty people from more than 40 countries were on board.

On Monday morning, armed Israeli naval commandos began intercepting the fleet in international waters west of Cyprus, about 250 nautical miles (460km) from the coast of Gaza, which is under an Israeli maritime blockade.

The GSF's organisers said all the boats had been intercepted by Tuesday evening, with one managing to get within 80 nautical miles of the Palestinian territory.

They accused Israel of an "illegal, high-seas aggression" and said Israeli commandos had opened fire at six boats, used water cannon, and intentionally rammed one vessel.

The Israeli foreign ministry said no live ammunition was used and insisted it would "not permit any breach of the lawful naval blockade on Gaza".

The ministry also said that all the activists had been transferred to Israeli vessels and that they would be allowed to meet their consular representatives after arriving in Israel.

On Wednesday morning, Adalah said the activists were being "taken into Israeli territory entirely against their will" and detained at Ashdod port.

"The legal team will challenge the legality of these detentions and demand the immediate release of all flotilla participants," it added.

In the afternoon, Ben-Gvir – an ultra-nationalist who, as national security minister, oversees Israel's police force – posted a video on social media, captioned "Welcome to Israel". It showed him visiting a detention facility at the...
body.zh: 国际社会谴责以色列对待前往加沙的援助船队上被以色列海军拦截的亲巴勒斯坦活动人士的方式。 美国、英国、法国、意大利和加拿大等国家对极右翼国家安全部长伊塔马尔·本格维尔发布一段视频表示愤怒，视频中他嘲笑跪下双手反绑的活动人士。 他的行为还引起了以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡的罕见批评，内塔尼亚胡表示这些行为“不符合以色列的价值观”。 代表被拘留者的人权组织表示，他们受到身体虐待，造成“严重、广泛的伤害”。 阿达拉说，至少三人被送往医院，随后出院。 “[阿达拉]的律师记录了数十名疑似肋骨骨折并导致呼吸困难的参与者，”它说。 “报告还表明，参与者经常使用泰瑟枪，以及在拦截过程中使用橡皮子弹造成的伤害...... 该组织表示，活动人士还“遭受严重贬低、性骚扰和羞辱”。 上周四，参加全球 Sumud 船队 (GSF) 的 50 多艘船只从土耳其出发，携带象征性的援助物资。船上有来自40多个国家的430人。 周一早上，武装的以色列海军突击队开始在塞浦路斯以西的国际水域拦截这支舰队，该水域距离加沙海岸约250海里（460公里），该地区正处于以色列海上封锁之下。 GSF的组织者表示，截至周二晚上，所有船只均已被拦截，其中一艘设法进入了距离巴勒斯坦领土80海里的范围。 他们指责以色列进行“非法的公海侵略”，并表示以色列突击队向六艘船只开火，使用高压水枪，并故意撞击一艘船只。 以色列外交部表示，没有使用实弹，并坚称“不会允许任何违反对加沙合法海军封锁的行为”。 外交部还表示，所有活动人士已被转移到以色列船只上，他们将被允许在抵达以色列后会见领事代表。 周三上午，阿达拉表示，这些活动人士“完全违背他们的意愿被带入以色列领土”，并被拘留在阿什杜德港。 声明补充说：“法律团队将质疑这些拘留的合法性，并要求立即释放所有船队参与者。” 下午，担任国家安全部长、负责监督以色列警察部队的极端民族主义者本-格维尔在社交媒体上发布了一段视频，标题为“欢迎来到以色列”。视频显示他参观了位于...的拘留所。

reflection.en: The act of taunting those in custody, even adversaries, reveals a profound lack of the compassion and respect that should characterize leadership. In moments of tension, the call to love our enemies challenges us to respond with dignity and restraint, rather than escalating hostility. This principle reminds us that true strength lies in extending grace,...
reflection.zh: 嘲讽被拘留者，即使是对手，也暴露出领导者应有的同情心和尊重严重缺失。在紧张时刻，爱仇敌的呼召挑战我们以尊严和克制回应，而不是升级敌意。这一原则提醒我们，真正的力量在于施予恩典，即使是对那些反对我们的人。

verse.textEn: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
verse.textZh: 要爱你们的仇敌，为那逼迫你们的祷告。

title.en: Sacred hall housing 'eternal flame' in Japan destroyed by fire
title.zh: 日本供奉“永恒之火”的圣殿被大火烧毁

summary.en: A sacred hall in Japan, housing an 'eternal flame,' was destroyed by fire. Authorities are investigating the cause, with reports suggesting the flame itself may have been responsible. The temple has successfully relocated the flame.
summary.zh: 日本一座供奉“永恒之火”的圣殿被大火烧毁。据报道，当局正在调查起火原因，并指出火灾可能由火焰本身引起。寺庙已将火焰转移至其他地点。

body.en:
A fire has destroyed the Reikado Hall on Miyajima island in the city of Hatsukaichi, Hiroshima Prefecture.

Reikado is part of the Daishoin Buddhist temple complex and houses the 'eternal flame', which the temple says has been burning for nearly 1,200 years.

The temple has moved the flame to a different location and authorities said the fire may have been caused by it, according to the Japan Times.

The fire was first reported on Wednesday morning and was confirmed extinguished on Thursday.

According to the Japan Times, the Reikado Hall also burned down in 2005 and the flame was preserved.

A North Korean women's football team played in South Korea marking the first time athletes from the North have crossed the border in nearly 8 years.

Pakistan says it hit 'military and terrorist infrastructure' - but the UN and victims' families reject this claim.

Officials said the group had been hiking up the active volcano despite a climbing ban.

A glamping facility was destroyed by the raging torrent in Bogor, West Java on 4 May.

As the US-Iran has sent the world scrambling for fuel, China is positioned to benefit from its rapid shift into electric vehicles.

The BBC’s Laura Bicker explains the economic costs and possible political wins for China brought on by the war.

Thousands of people have been displaced after a fire destroyed around 1,000 homes in Malaysia's Sabah state.

Robots competed in a half marathon race in Beijing on Sunday, with the winning machine leaving its human rivals for dust.

The escape of Neukgu, a two-year-old wolf, from a zoo in the city of Daejon captured national attention.

The Philippine President challenged anyone questioning his fitness to join him in the gym.

K-pop stars BTS kicked off their marathon world tour in South Korea, with a heavy nod to their new album Arirang.

The megastars kick off their grandest tour, the largest in K-pop history, in Seoul on Thursday after a nearly four-year hiatus.

BBC News Asia Business Correspondent Suranajana Tewari spoke to people taking to the streets of Manila.

Some 260,000 fans are expected to watch BTS perform together on Saturday for the first time since 2022.

A Lakshmi goddess shrine at Bangkok shopping mall has become a place where young people come to pray for love.

It's the first election since the 2024 Gen Z uprising that toppled Bangladesh's long-serving prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

The pro-democracy media tycoon was sentenced to 20 years in jail by the Hong Kong High Court.

At least 31 people have been killed after a suicide bomber detonated a device at a Shia mosque, according to police.

A mayor in the Philippines has survived a rocket launcher attack on his vehicle in broad daylight.

Correspondent Jonathan Head says the 'devastating' accident is an enormous...
body.zh: 广岛县廿日市宫岛的礼华堂被大火烧毁。 灵华堂是大圣院佛教寺庙建筑群的一部分，拥有“永恒的火焰”，寺庙称这股火焰已经燃烧了近 1,200 年。 据《日本时报》报道，该寺庙已将火苗移至其他地点，当局称火灾可能是由该寺庙引起的。 火灾于周三早上首次报道，并于周四确认被扑灭。 据《日本时报》报道，礼华堂也于2005年被烧毁，火焰得以保存。 朝鲜女子足球队在韩国比赛，这是近八年来朝鲜运动员首次跨越边境。 巴基斯坦称其袭击了“军事和恐怖主义基础设施”，但联合国和受害者家属否认了这一说法。 官员们表示，尽管有攀登禁令，该组织仍在攀登活火山。 5 月 4 日，西爪哇省茂物市的一处豪华露营设施被汹涌的洪流摧毁。 随着美国和伊朗的冲突导致世界争夺燃料，中国有望从其向电动汽车的快速转变中受益。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的劳拉·比克 (Laura Bicker) 解释了战争给中国带来的经济成本和可能的政治胜利。 马来西亚沙巴州发生火灾，烧毁了约 1,000 所房屋，导致数千人流离失所。 周日，机器人在北京参加了一场半程马拉松比赛，获胜的机器将人类对手远远甩在身后。 两岁大的狼 Neukgu 从大田市动物园逃跑引起了全国关注。 菲律宾总统要求任何质疑他健康状况的人都和他一起去健身房。 韩国流行歌星防弹少年团 (BTS) 在韩国拉开了马拉松世界巡演的序幕，向他们的新专辑《阿里郎》致敬。 经过近四年的中断后，这些巨星将于周四在首尔开始他们最盛大的巡演，这也是韩国流行音乐历史上规模最大的巡演。 BBC 新闻亚洲商业记者 Suranajana Tewari 向走上马尼拉街头的人们发表讲话。 周六，预计将有约 26 万粉丝观看 BTS 自 2022 年以来的首次共同表演。 曼谷购物中心的一座拉克希米女神神社已成为年轻人前来祈求爱情的地方。 这是自 2024 年 Z 世代起义推翻孟加拉国长期任职的总理谢赫·哈西娜以来的首次选举。 这位亲民主媒体大亨被香港高等法院判处20年监禁。 据警方称，一名自杀式炸弹袭击者在什叶派清真寺引爆装置，造成至少 31 人死亡。 菲律宾一名市长的车辆在光天化日之下遭到火箭发射器袭击，幸免于难。 记者乔纳森·海德表示，这次“毁灭性”事故是一场巨大的……

reflection.en: The destruction of a sacred hall and its 'eternal flame' reminds us of the transient nature of all earthly things, even those we hold most sacred. While human traditions and symbols can be meaningful, they are ultimately fragile and cannot compare to the one true God, who alone is eternal and unchanging. This event invites us to reflect on where we place...
reflection.zh: 一座圣殿及其“永恒之火”被毁，提醒我们世间万物的短暂性，即使是我们视为最神圣的事物也不例外。虽然人类的传统和象征可能意义深远，但它们终究是脆弱的，无法与独一的真神相比，唯有祂是永恒不变的。这一事件邀请我们反思，我们最终的信任和敬拜究竟归于何处。

verse.textEn: You shall have no other gods before me.
verse.textZh: 除了我以外，你不可有别的神。

title.en: 'Great triangle reversed': Xi met Trump, then Putin. It showed the world could be shifting
title.zh: “大三角”逆转：习近平会见特朗普，然后是普京。这表明世界可能正在发生转变

summary.en: The Chinese president held meetings with two global leaders, one focused on economic agreements and the other on geopolitical tensions, indicating a potential shift in international dynamics.
summary.zh: 中国国家主席与两位全球领导人举行了会晤，其中一次会议侧重于经济协议，另一次则聚焦于地缘政治对抗，这预示着国际格局可能正在发生转变。

body.en:
Peking duck, Chinese opera and Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake — this was Chinese leader Xi Jinping's grand welcome for his "old friend", Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Not seeing you for one day feels like being apart for three autumns," Putin told Xi, a saying from one of China's oldest poetry collections, as they met in Beijing.

The friendly exchange took place in the Great Hall of the People, an imposing building on Tiananmen Square that houses China's legislature, the same spot where United States President Donald Trump stood less than a week ago .

The timing of the back-to-back meetings might have been coincidental, as Trump postponed an earlier summit in March to stay in the US during the war in Iran.

"These two visits reveal a deeper structural shift in global politics," Alexander Korolev, senior lecturer in politics and international relations at UNSW Sydney, told SBS News.

"China, I think, is increasingly becoming the central node ... We can call it a great triangle reversed, or we can probably call it a great triangle with Chinese characteristics.

"During the Cold War, the United States was the apex of the great triangle, but now it is flipped, and China is sitting at the top of the triangle," he said.

"It's not that China is trying to put Washington and Moscow against each other, but it's increasingly positioning itself as the centre of the system, the place where major power diplomacy must pass."

Putin's meeting with Xi did not go entirely as the Russians would likely have hoped, as he failed to secure a deal for the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline, which will transport gas from Siberia to China if it goes ahead.

Russian officials said both sides had reached a "general understanding on the parameters" of the project.

The leaders also issued a joint statement, outlining plans to expand collaboration across various fields, from artificial intelligence to the conservation of rare species such as tigers, leopards, and pandas.

Edward Chan, a postdoctoral fellow of China Studies at the Australian National University, said the meeting "is likely to underscore continuity in the China–Russia relationship".

"Xi wanted to remain committed to its partnership with Putin. This was reflected in the joint statement, which continued to emphasise the China–Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination," he told SBS News.

"In that sense, the meeting was seen more as a reaffirmation of the China–Russia relationship amid the US–China stabilised great power relationship."

Xi and Putin also criticised Trump's Golden Dome missile defence shield — a space-based missile interceptor system.

The criticism came almost a week after Trump described Xi as a "great leader" and said it was an "honour" to be...
body.zh: 北京烤鸭、中国戏曲、柴可夫斯基的《天鹅湖》——这是中国领导人习近平对“老朋友”俄罗斯总统普京的隆重欢迎。 普京在北京会面时对习近平说：“一日不见，犹如三秋别离。”这是中国最古老的诗集之一中的一句话。 这次友好交流是在人民大会堂举行的，这是一座位于天安门广场上的宏伟建筑，是中国立法机关的所在地，不到一周前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普也曾站过这里。 连续举行会议的时间可能纯属巧合，因为特朗普推迟了三月份的峰会，以便在伊朗战争期间留在美国。 “这两次访问揭示了全球政治更深层次的结构性转变，”悉尼新南威尔士大学政治和国际关系高级讲师亚历山大·科罗廖夫告诉SBS新闻。 “我认为，中国正在日益成为中心节点……我们可以称之为倒转大三角，也可以称之为具有中国特色的大三角。 他说：“冷战期间，美国是大三角的顶点，但现在它翻转了，中国坐在三角的顶端。” “中国并不是试图让华盛顿和莫斯科相互对立，而是越来越将自己定位为体系的中心，是大国外交的必经之地。” 普京与习近平的会晤并没有完全像俄罗斯人希望的那样进行，因为他未能就西伯利亚力量2号管道达成协议，该管道如果顺利进行，将把天然气从西伯利亚输送到中国。 俄罗斯官员表示，双方已就该项目的“参数达成总体谅解”。 领导人还发表了联合声明，概述了扩大各个领域合作的计划，从人工智能到保护老虎、豹子和熊猫等稀有物种。 澳大利亚国立大学中国研究博士后研究员爱德华·陈表示，这次会议“可能会强调中俄关系的连续性”。 “习近平希望继续致力于与普京的伙伴关系。这在联合声明中得到了体现，联合声明继续强调中俄全面战略协作伙伴关系，”他告诉SBS新闻。 “从这个意义上说，这次会晤更多地被视为在美中稳定的大国关系中对中俄关系的重申。” 习近平和普京还批评了特朗普的金顶导弹防御系统——一种天基导弹拦截系统。 近一周前，特朗普将习近平描述为“伟大的领导人”，并表示很“荣幸”……

While complete harmony may not always be achievable, the pursuit of peaceful...
reflection.zh: 国际关系常常需要在合作与分歧管理之间取得微妙的平衡。圣经中“若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦”的呼召，提醒着各国领导人和国家，在复杂的全球动态中，持续努力是必要的。尽管完全的和睦并非总能实现，但追求和平共处仍然是一个重要的愿望。

title.en: Australia endorses historic UN resolution for climate change accountability
title.zh: 澳大利亚支持联合国具有历史意义的气候变化问责决议

summary.en: Australia voted to endorse a UN advisory opinion on climate change accountability, despite being a major global exporter of coal and gas.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚投票支持联合国关于气候变化问责制的咨询意见，尽管该国是全球主要的煤炭和天然气出口国之一。

body.en:
Australia has voted in favour of a landmark United Nations resolution, spearheaded by its Pacific island neighbours, urging action on climate change.

The 193-member global body endorsed an advisory opinion provided by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Wednesday, which notably warns that the failure to curb fossil fuel production could constitute an "internationally wrongful act".

The hard-fought legal opinion from the world's top court , delivered in July 2025, was first conceived by a group of Pacific students.

The Pacific island nation of Vanuatu was the first to act in support of the opinion.

The climate-vulnerable island nation, supported by its Pacific allies, was also the first to sponsor the UN General Assembly resolution.

The resolution passed with 141 votes in favour, eight against and 28 abstentions.

Pacific Islands Students Fighting Climate Change director Vishal Prasad is one of the students who instigated the ICJ advisory opinion.

"This must be a turning point in accountability for damaging the climate," he said.

"Communities on the frontlines, like in the Pacific, have been waiting far too long and continue to pay too high a price for the actions of others."

Amanda McKenzie, chief executive of the Australia-based Climate Council, said the ruling exposes the federal government's stance on fossil fuel exports.

"While the government is ramping up renewable power, it is still giving fossil fuel giants a free ride," she said.

"Continuing to wave through massive new coal and gas projects puts our kids' future at risk and is now clearly against international law."

The nation remains a major exporter of coal and gas, despite pursuing significant domestic emissions cuts and ambitious renewables targets.

Other big fossil fuel producers, including the United States, Russia, Iran and Saudi Arabia, opposed the measure.

Australia was not among the resolution's 69 co-sponsors leading into the vote. Australia and New Zealand were the only Pacific nations missing from the list.

Australia holds a key president of negotiations role heading into the next Conference of the Parties climate change talks to be held in Türkiye, with Fiji and Tuvalu set to hold official pre-event meetings.

Low-lying Tuvalu is expected to lose 90 per cent of its land to the ocean by the end of the century due to sea level rise.

The UN General Assembly resolution formally reaffirms the ICJ's findings and urges governments to align policies with limiting global warming to 1.5C.

It also urges nations in violation to provide reparation for damage and calls for the regulation of fossil fuel companies.

body.zh: 澳大利亚投票赞成由其太平洋岛屿邻国牵头的一项具有里程碑意义的联合国决议，敦促采取行动应对气候变化。 这个拥有 193 个成员国的全球机构周三认可了国际法院 (ICJ) 提供的咨询意见，该意见特别警告说，未能遏制化石燃料生产可能构成“国际不法行为”。 世界最高法院于 2025 年 7 月发表的经过艰苦斗争的法律意见，最初是由一群太平洋学生提出的。 太平洋岛国瓦努阿图最先表态支持这一观点。 这个气候脆弱的岛国在其太平洋盟友的支持下，也是第一个提出联合国大会决议的国家。 该决议以 141 票赞成、8 票反对、28 票弃权获得通过。 太平洋岛屿学生应对气候变化主任维沙尔·普拉萨德（Vishal Prasad）是发起国际法院咨询意见的学生之一。 “这必定是对破坏气候的责任追究的一个转折点，”他说。 “像太平洋地区一样，前线的社区已经等待太久，并继续为其他人的行为付出过高的代价。” 澳大利亚气候委员会首席执行官阿曼达·麦肯齐表示，这一裁决暴露了联邦政府对化石燃料出口的立场。 “虽然政府正在加大可再生能源发电的力度，但它仍然在给化石燃料巨头搭便车，”她说。 “继续大规模的新煤炭和天然气项目会让我们孩子的未来面临风险，现在显然违反了国际法。” 尽管追求大幅国内减排和雄心勃勃的可再生能源目标，但该国仍然是煤炭和天然气的主要出口国。 其他大型化石燃料生产国，包括美国、俄罗斯、伊朗和沙特阿拉伯，反对这项措施。 澳大利亚并不在该决议的 69 个共同提案国之列。澳大利亚和新西兰是唯一未出现在该名单中的太平洋国家。 澳大利亚在即将于土耳其举行的下一次缔约方大会气候变化谈判中担任关键的谈判主席，斐济和图瓦卢将举行正式的会前会议。 由于海平面上升，地势低洼的图瓦卢预计到本世纪末将失去 90% 的土地。 联合国大会决议正式重申了国际法院的调查结果，并敦促各国政府调整政策，将全球变暖幅度限制在 1.5 摄氏度以内。 它还敦促违规国家提供损害赔偿，并呼吁对化石燃料公司进行监管。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: Samsung strike on hold as workers push for AI bonus
title.zh: 三星罢工暂停，工人争取人工智能奖金

summary.en: Samsung workers have suspended a planned strike to vote on a provisional agreement. The walkout was initially scheduled for Thursday as union members sought an AI bonus.
summary.zh: 三星工人已暂停原定罢工，以对一项临时协议进行投票。此次罢工原定于周四开始，此前工会成员一直在争取人工智能奖金。

body.en:
The largest union at Samsung Electronics has suspended a planned strike after reaching a last-minute tentative pay agreement with the South Korean technology giant.

It has temporarily eased fears of disruption at the world's largest memory chipmaker during a boom in the building of artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

The union, which represents nearly 48,000 workers, said industrial action that was due to begin on Thursday would be suspended while members vote on the deal from 22-27 May.

The dispute centres on how to distribute profits generated by soaring demand for AI memory chips.

At issue is the distribution of bonuses between staff in memory chip divisions and those in other units.

Samsung had planned to pay generous bonuses to 27,000 staff making memory chips – at least six times more than its workers making other chips, and electronics.

The union said that 23,000 workers who were making less advanced chips for companies like Tesla and Nvidia should not be left behind.

It raised concerns over potential disruption to chip production, with major implications for global supply chains and South Korea's export-driven economy.

Samsung is the world's largest memory chipmaker by sales and a major supplier of chips used in AI data centres, smartphones and laptops.

The broader Samsung Group accounts for roughly a fifth of South Korea's economic output.

The dispute comes at a sensitive moment for the company as it faces intensifying competition from rivals SK Hynix and Micron amid surging AI-driven chip demand that has already strained global supply.

Samsung's operating profit in the January to March quarter jumped about 750% from a year earlier.

Booming demand for AI chips pushed its stock market market valuation past $1tn (£744bn) in May.

This led to bonuses more than three times higher than those offered to Samsung employees. Some Samsung workers jumped ship to SK Hynix as a result.

Samsung then proposed that memory chip workers receive bonuses of 607% of their annual salary – higher than SK Hynix - according to transcripts of wage negotiations seen by Reuters.

But employees in other businesses would only receive bonuses of 50% to 100%, according to the documents.

The union also wanted Samsung to abolish a bonus cap of 50% of annual salaries and allocate 15% of annual operating profit to a bonus pool distributed to workers.

Samsung bosses previously flagged that the strike could impact South Korea's economy more broadly, because of lower sales, investment outflows and lower tax revenue.

In the statement issued after the tentative deal was agreed the company said: "With a humble attitude, we will build a more mature and constructive labour-management relationship to ensure that such an incident never happens again."

title.en: Israel envoy says Ben-Gvir not reflective of country, as activist treatment condemned
title.zh: 黄英贤谴责以色列拘留活动人士的待遇“令人震惊且不可接受”

summary.en: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong condemned the treatment of activists detained by Israel as "shocking and unacceptable." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also stated that the treatment of the activists by Itamar Ben-Gvir was wrong.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤谴责以色列对待被拘留活动人士的方式“令人震惊且不可接受”。以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡也表示，伊塔马尔·本-格维尔对待这些活动人士的做法是错误的。

body.en:
Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, has joined growing condemnation of the actions of Israel's far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir after he posted a video overnight showing detained activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla kneeling with their hands tied and foreheads on the ground.

The video, shared on X by Ben-Gvir, has drawn international condemnation. It was published after Israeli forces intercepted the flotilla's vessels at sea and began detaining hundreds of foreign activists at the southern port of Ashdod.

Newman told journalists Ben-Gvir's actions had been broadly condemned by the Israeli government and were not reflective of the government.

"He does not reflect the values of the state of Israel. He has been condemned by the prime minister, by the foreign minister, the entire leadership of the state of Israel.

"A country is not measured by the actions of one politician, but how the government responds to actions which are disgraceful."

Newman said that because his actions had been condemned, debate around Ben-Gvir should be put aside "and we address the real issue, which is the flotilla itself".

He repeated claims made by the Israeli government that the flotilla was a "provocation".

Earlier, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the images of Ben-Gvir were "shocking and unacceptable".

"We condemn the actions of Israeli Minister Ben-Gvir — who Australia has sanctioned — and the degrading actions of Israeli authorities towards those detained," she said in a statement.

"I have asked Australia's Ambassador to Israel to make representations to Israel, reiterating our call for the release of the detained Australians and for Israel to ensure no ill treatment of any detainees and to act in line with international obligations."

She said Newman had been called in to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade to "reinforce this message".

Flotilla organisers had called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to join international condemnation of the footage, calling on the government to summon or send home Israel's ambassador to Australia.

"We are deeply concerned for all 318 participants, the 11 courageous Australian friends and their families," the Australian delegation of the Global Sumud Flotilla said in a statement.

"There's absolutely no need or no place for it, and you know, when it comes to people who are engaged in that journey, obviously our departments tried to discourage people from going down that path, but having gone down that path, they should be treated humanely.

"I can only imagine what it's like to be a parent or a loved one of one of the people involved in that trip, and to see them treat them being treated that way, I think is deeply disappointing."

body.zh: 外交部长黄英贤谴责了以色列极右翼安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔的行为，此前他隔夜发布了一段视频，显示来自加沙的船队中被拘留的活动人士双手被绑，额头着地跪着。 Ben-Gvir 在 X 上分享的这段视频引起了国际社会的谴责。这篇文章是在以色列军队在海上拦截该船队的船只并开始在南部阿什杜德港拘留数百名外国活动人士之后发表的。 她在一份声明中表示：“我们谴责以色列部长本-格维尔的行为——澳大利亚已对他实施制裁——以及以色列当局对被拘留者采取的有辱人格的行为。” “我已要求澳大利亚驻以色列大使向以色列提出交涉，再次呼吁释放被拘留的澳大利亚人，并呼吁以色列确保不虐待任何被拘留者，并按照国际义务行事。” 船队组织者呼吁总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯加入国际社会对这段视频的谴责，并呼吁政府召见或遣返以色列驻堪培拉大使。 Global Sumud 船队澳大利亚代表团在一份声明中表示：“我们对所有 318 名参与者、11 位勇敢的澳大利亚朋友及其家人深表关切。” 视频标题为“欢迎来到以色列”，视频显示数十名活动人士被迫双手被绑、额头着地跪下。有时，可以听到以色列国歌的背景音乐。 视频还显示，本-格维尔在被拘留的活动人士中质问并挥舞着以色列国旗。 美国驻以色列大使迈克·哈卡比谴责他所说的“卑鄙行为”。 赫卡比在 X 上写道：“以色列每一位高级官员都对本·格维尔的卑鄙行为表示普遍的愤怒和谴责。舰队是愚蠢的噱头，但本·格维尔背叛了他国家的尊严。” 欧盟委员哈贾·拉赫比卜 (Hadja Lahbib) 也批评了本·格维尔 (Ben-Gvir)，他在 X 上表示，“任何人都不应该因为捍卫人类而受到惩罚”。 法国表示，已就本格维尔的“不可接受的行为”召见以色列大使，而马德里则谴责对活动人士的“可怕”待遇，并表示以色列临时代办也被召见以示抗议。 比利时因一段“令人深感不安”的视频而召见以色列大使。 加拿大总理马克·卡尼表示，“舰队上平民受到的恶劣待遇……是不可接受的”，并补充说外交部长已指示官员传唤以色列大使。 爱尔兰外交部长海伦·麦肯蒂表示，她对这段视频感到“震惊和震惊”，并要求立即释放这些活动人士，其中包括妹妹……

title.en: Iran examines US proposal as Donald Trump says negotiations are in 'final stage'
title.zh: 伊朗审查美国提案，特朗普称谈判进入“最后阶段”

summary.en: US President Donald Trump announced that negotiations between the United States and Iran are nearing their conclusion, with Iran currently reviewing the US proposal.
summary.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普表示，美国和伊朗之间的谈判已进入最后阶段，伊朗正在审查美国的提案。

body.en:
Iran said on Thursday AEST it was examining the latest United States proposal received from mediator Pakistan in talks to end the war in the Middle East, despite the two sides trading threats about resuming attacks.

It came after US President Donald Trump told reporters that the US was in the "final stages" of negotiations with Iran.

"We'll either have a deal or we're going to do some things that are a little bit nasty. But hopefully that won't happen," Trump said.

"I'm in no hurry. I just, ideally, I'd like to see few people killed, as opposed to a lot," he added.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said the Islamic Republic had "received the points of view of the American side and we are currently examining them".

He reiterated Iran's demands, including the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad and an end to the US blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf had said earlier that the US wanted to restart the war, after Trump said he would attack again unless Iran agreed to a peace deal.

Ghalibaf, who warned of a "forceful response", was speaking after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said any renewed war would spread far beyond the Middle East.

"The enemy's movements, both overt and clandestine, show that despite economic and political pressure, it has not abandoned its military objectives and is seeking to start a new war," Ghalibaf said.

A ceasefire on 8 April brought a halt to the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has roiled the global economy, but with both countries seemingly reluctant to resume the fighting, a war of words has taken its place.

Trump has repeatedly threatened Iran with renewed military action, while Iranian officials have hit back with their own warnings.

The Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday: "If the aggression against Iran is repeated, the promised regional war will this time spread far beyond the region, and our devastating blows will crush you."

Nevertheless, despite sporadic bursts of violence, the two countries have continued to take part in diplomatic exchanges, mediated by Pakistan, aimed at bringing a formal end to the war.

Citing diplomatic sources, Iran's official IRNA news agency announced a visit to Tehran by Pakistan's interior minister, his second in less than a week.

Saudi foreign minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan praised Trump on Wednesday for his decision to "give diplomacy a chance" and urged Iran to seize "the opportunity to avoid the dangerous implications of escalation".

Israel's army chief, Lieutenant Colonel Eyal Zamir, said the military was at its highest alert level "and prepared for any development".

title.en: Montenegro at 20: EU ambitions and Serbian ties
title.zh: 黑山共和国20周年：欧盟雄心与塞尔维亚关系

summary.en: Twenty years after seceding from the state union with Serbia, Montenegro is seen as a Western Balkan frontrunner for EU membership but remains marked by corruption, unresolved divisions and Serbia's political influence.
summary.zh: 黑山共和国在脱离与塞尔维亚的国家联盟二十年后，被视为西巴尔干地区加入欧盟的领跑者，但仍受腐败、未解决的分歧以及塞尔维亚政治影响的困扰。

body.en:
Twenty years after seceding from the state union with Serbia, Montenegro is seen as a Western Balkan frontrunner for EU membership but remains marked by corruption, unresolved divisions and Serbia's political influence.

On May 21,  Montenegro will mark two decades since the historic referendum that paved the way for its secession from its state union with  Serbia .

The anniversary celebrations will take place in an atmosphere shaped by the country's reputation as the Western Balkans ' "high achiever" in the EU accession process.

Over the past few years, Podgorica has managed to kick-start its stalled EU accession talks, speed up reforms and position itself as the frontrunner in the region to join the EU at a time when Brussels has renewed its interest in bringing new members into the bloc.

"It's easy to be the star pupil in a classroom of bad students," Daliborka Uljarevic of the Centre for Civic Education in Podgorica told DW.

Her remark reflects the broader regional context. While much of the Western Balkans has stagnated, or even regressed, on the path toward the European Union , Montenegro has managed to capitalize on the geopolitical momentum created by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the EU's renewed focus on enlargement .

Montenegro declared independence from Serbia in 2006 after a tightly contested, high-turnout referendum in which 55.5% of voters backed leaving the union with Serbia.

For the next 14 years, the country was ruled by the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) led by longtime strongman Milo Djukanovic.

Over the years, Djukanovic's government faced repeated accusations of corruption and links between political elites and organized crime, while critics increasingly described Montenegro as a "captured state."

The DPS eventually lost power in 2020 after months of mass protests and church-led rallies against a controversial religious property law, in what became the first democratic transfer of power since independence.

"Montenegro is one of the rare countries in the region that had enough democratic capacity to replace a man who had been in power for so long without major upheaval," said Aleksandar Popov of the Center for Regionalism in Novi Sad, Serbia. "If we look at Serbia, that will be much harder to achieve," he told DW.

Montenegro's political scene is still marked by a pro-sovereignty/pro-Serbian divide that has shaped the country since independence.

One side emphasizes a distinct Montenegrin national identity and statehood, while the other sees Montenegrins as part of the broader Serbian national body and favors close political, cultural and religious ties with the country's northeastern neighbor.

reflection.en: Montenegro's journey highlights the complex path nations face in building a stable and prosperous future. While aspiring to join the EU, it grapples with internal challenges like corruption and unresolved divisions. Proverbs 14:34 reminds us that a nation's moral character profoundly impacts its standing and well-being.

title.en: In Iran, internet access becomes a luxury for the few
title.zh: 在伊朗，互联网接入成为少数人的奢侈品

summary.en: Officials in Iran have implemented an internet blockade, making full access to online information and communication a paid privilege available only to select groups. This policy effectively turns essential digital access into a luxury.
summary.zh: 尽管伊朗持续实施互联网封锁，但少数特定群体仍能付费获得“专业互联网”服务。获取信息和通信正日益成为一种奢侈品。

body.en:
Despite the ongoing internet blockade in Iran, access to "Internet-Pro" is available to select groups for a fee. Access to information and communication is increasingly becoming a luxury.

Iran's National Security Council recently approved a plan to grant certain groups paid internet access, albeit with a daily usage limit on foreign websites and international data traffic.

The internet in Iran has been shut down since the US and Israel launched attacks on the country on February 28.

"Internet Pro" does not refer to a technical upgrade but allows users standard internet access that bypasses the block.

According to journalist and internet researcher Solmaz Eikder, major platforms such as Instagram, X and YouTube — which have long been blocked in Iran — still cannot be used even by many "Internet Pro" users without a Virtual Private Network (VPN).

Eikder has been living in exile in Europe for five years. She works for Filterbaan, also known as Filterwatch, an Iranian digital rights organization that monitors  internet censorship , digital repression and surveillance in Iran. The findings are frequently used by journalists, activists and researchers who study digital repression in Iran.

The current shutdown, which has now lasted for more than 80 days, is the longest yet in Iran , but not the first of its kind.

For years, the Iranian security apparatus has used this method to disrupt communication between Iranians and cutting off the outside world. This most recently occurred during nationwide protests in January, which the regime brutally suppressed.

Millions of people are now once again cut off from the digital economy and communication.

According to government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani, "Internet Pro" is intended to "prevent disruptions to economic activity and ensure business communication in times of crisis."

The service is offered to certain professional groups, such as members of the Chamber of Commerce, startups, technology companies and retailers. They receive an initial package of 50 gigabytes of data, which costs the equivalent of about $11 (around €9.5).

"That's a lot of money in Iran," said Eikder. Since the war began, many households have been under growing economic pressure. Inflation has risen to over 50% and the rial has plunged, which has led to a sharp increase in prices for basic necessities.

Destroyed industrial facilities and massive production losses have hit the economy hard. Tens of thousands of jobs have been lost.

Furthermore, millions of smaller income sources have been wiped out by internet blocks .

title.en: Who gets convicted in Nigeria's anti-corruption war?
title.zh: 尼日利亚反腐战争中谁被定罪？

summary.en: The recent conviction of Nigeria's former power minister, Saleh Mamman, has reignited discussions about accountability within the country's anti-corruption efforts.
summary.zh: 尼日利亚前电力部长萨利赫·马曼最近被定罪，重新引发了关于该国反腐斗争中问责制问题的辩论。

body.en:
The recent conviction of ex-power minister Saleh Mamman has rekindled debate over who is held accountable in Nigeria.

Saleh Mamman, a former Nigerian minister of power was arrested on Tuesday, days after he was sentenced in absentia to 75 years in prison for laundering 33.8 billion naira ($24.6 million), in what was widely described as a rare high-profile conviction.

Prosecutors said the funds were proceeds of unlawful activity linked to government-financed hydroelectric projects , including Nigeria's Mambilla and Zungerupower plants.

Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) chief Ola Olukoyede said ​that Mamman, who had been in hiding since ​his May 7 conviction, was arrested in ​the ‌northern Nigerian city of Kaduna and was now in custody. 

Mamman had served as minister of power between 2015 and 2021, at a time when then-President Muhammadu Buhari's administration had vowed to fight corruption . The judge also ordered him to pay back an outstanding sum of 22 billion naira to the state.

Weeks earlier, former acting accountant-general Chukwunyere Nwabuoku was handed a 72-year prison sentence after being convicted of money laundering.

They joined a growing list of former public officials prosecuted over corruption allegations running into billions of naira.

Nigeria's anti-graft agency, the EFCC, recently declared the former Humanitarian Affairs Minister wanted over alleged abuse of office and diversion of public funds.

But beyond this, there are broader questions about who actually gets convicted in Nigeria's justice system .

Corruption cases against public officials in Nigeria often stall in the courts, sometimes taking years — or even decades — to conclude.

According to a review of 393 corruption cases between 2013 and 2026 by Dataphyte, a research organization, only 144 have reached final judgment, leaving more than 60% still pending at various stages of trial.

These cases, spanning 14 years, are linked to 3.61 trillion naira, $1.33 billion, and €26,170 in alleged corruption.

"Further analysis shows that most cases concluded so far involve appointed officials, suggesting that convictions are less common among those elected into office than those appointed," Dataphyte said.

Reporting by Nigerian news portal TheCable underscores this disparity. While 33 former governors have been prosecuted, only six have been convicted. Some convictions were later overturned on appeal or pardoned. 

Analysts say recent convictions of senior public officials may signal a push towards greater accountability efforts.

However, David Alechenu, a team lead at the Nigeria Anti-Corruption Agencies Strengthening Project, cautioned that "isolated convictions alone are not enough to conclude that the anti-corruption fight has become...
body.zh: 前电力部长萨利赫·马曼 (Saleh Mamman) 最近被定罪，重新引发了尼日利亚关于谁应承担责任的争论。 尼日利亚前权力部长萨利赫·马曼 (Saleh Mamman) 于周二被捕，几天前，他因洗钱 338 亿奈拉（合 2,460 万美元）被缺席判处 75 年监禁，这被广泛认为是罕见的高调定罪。 检察官表示，这些资金是与政府资助的水力发电项目相关的非法活动的收益，这些项目包括尼日利亚的曼比拉和宗格鲁发电厂。 经济和金融犯罪委员会 (EFCC) 主席 Ola Olukoyede 表示，自 5 月 7 日定罪以来一直躲藏起来的 Mamman 在尼日利亚北部城市卡杜纳被捕，目前已被拘留。 马曼在 2015 年至 2021 年间担任权力部长，当时时任总统穆罕默德·布哈里的政府发誓要打击腐败。法官还命令他向国家偿还未偿还的 220 亿奈拉。 几周前，前代理总会计师 Chukwunyere Nwabuoku 因洗钱罪被判处 72 年监禁。 他们加入了越来越多因腐败指控而被起诉的前公职人员名单，涉案金额达数十亿奈拉。 尼日利亚反腐败机构 EFCC 最近宣布前人道主义事务部长因涉嫌滥用职权和挪用公共资金而受到通缉。 但除此之外，还存在更广泛的问题，即谁实际上在尼日利亚司法系统中被定罪。 尼日利亚针对公职人员的腐败案件经常在法庭上陷入僵局，有时需要数年甚至数十年才能结案。 研究机构Dataphyte对2013年至2026年期间的393起腐败案件进行了审查，只有144起案件已做出最终判决，60%以上仍处于不同审判阶段。 这些案件历时 14 年，涉及 3.61 万亿奈拉、13.3 亿美元和 26,170 欧元的腐败指控。 Dataphyte 表示：“进一步的分析表明，迄今为止结案的大多数案件都涉及任命官员，这表明当选官员中的定罪情况比任命官员中少。” 尼日利亚新闻门户网站 TheCable 的报道强调了这种差异。虽然 33 名前州长被起诉，但只有 6 人被定罪。一些定罪后来在上诉中被推翻或被赦免。 分析人士表示，最近对高级公职人员的定罪可能预示着将加大问责力度。 然而，尼日利亚反腐败机构加强项目的团队负责人戴维·阿莱切努（David Alechenu）警告说，“仅个别定罪不足以得出反腐败斗争已成为……的结论。”

reflection.en: The debate surrounding accountability in Nigeria's anti-corruption efforts reminds us of the enduring call for leaders to act justly. Micah 6:8 asks what 雅伟 requires: to act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly. This conviction, and the ensuing public discussion, highlights the ongoing societal yearning for integrity and fair governance.

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.

title.en: Turkey targets press freedom in trial of DW's Alican Uludag
title.zh: 土耳其在德国之声记者阿利詹·乌鲁达格的审判中打击新闻自由

summary.en: DW correspondent Alican Uludag has been held in Turkey for three months, facing charges including "insulting the president." He is scheduled for his first court appearance via video link.
summary.zh: 德国之声记者阿利詹·乌鲁达格在土耳其被拘留三个月，部分指控是“侮辱总统”。他将于周四首次通过视频连线出庭受审。

body.en:
DW correspondent Alican Uludag has been in custody in Turkey for three months, in part on charges of "insulting the president." He is set to appear in court for the first time on Thursday, though only via video link.

DW correspondent Alican Uludag , accused of publicly insulting President Recep Tayyip Erdogan , spreading misleading information and disparaging state institutions in a total of 22 social media posts, will appear in court for the first time on Thursday.

Uludag was arrested at his apartment in Ankara  on February 19 and transferred to Istanbul, where he was placed in pre-trial detention. Although he is being held in Istanbul , his trial is taking place in Ankara. Despite his specific request to present his defense in person, Uludag is only allowed to participate in the proceedings via video conference.

Uludag's case is considered particularly noteworthy, as he is one of the few remaining journalists in Turkey  who focus on reporting on the judiciary and court proceedings.

Following his arrest, DW Director-General Barbara Massing dismissed the allegations against him as baseless. She called his arrest a "targeted attempt at intimidation," and said his case demonstrated "the extent to which the government is massively repressing  press freedom ." Massing emphasized that Uludag has an excellent network and access to key sources. From the government's perspective, she said, this is precisely what could make him an inconvenient and potentially dangerous voice.

Erol Onderoglu, the Turkey representative for press freedom watchdog Reporters Without Borders (RSF), said Uludag was being "arbitrarily targeted by a judiciary beholden to those in power." He added that Uludag, who he described as a "serious journalist known for his investigations into matters of public interest," may have angered those in power with his investigations.

Uludag himself considers his arrest a deliberate attempt to keep him from continuing his work. He had previously reported on contradictions in indictments and inconsistencies in key witness testimonies, on topics he claims to have covered impartially.

"I have not strayed from my journalistic work. I believe that the majority of members of the judiciary are themselves concerned about the increasingly politicized proceedings," he said. "I will continue to pursue the truth. I do not admit to any of the charges."

The journalist also described his time in custody as a paradoxical experience. While the opportunity to observe daily prison life and the mental state of inmates up close is personally difficult, he said, it is at the same time journalistically significant for his work as a justice reporter.

body.zh: 德国之声记者阿利坎·乌鲁达已在土耳其被拘留三个月，部分罪名是“侮辱总统”。他定于周四首次出庭，但仅通过视频链接出庭。 德国之声记者阿里坎·乌卢达格 (Alican Uludag) 将于周四首次出庭，他被指控在总共 22 条社交媒体帖子中公开侮辱总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安 (Recep Tayyip Erdogan)、传播误导性信息并贬低国家机构。 2 月 19 日，乌鲁达在安卡拉的公寓被捕，并被转移到伊斯坦布尔，并在那里受到审前拘留。尽管他被关押在伊斯坦布尔，但对他的审判却在安卡拉进行。尽管乌鲁达特别要求亲自出庭辩护，但他只能通过视频会议参加诉讼程序。 乌鲁达的案件被认为特别值得注意，因为他是土耳其仅存的少数专注于报道司法和法庭诉讼的记者之一。 在他被捕后，德国之声总干事芭芭拉·马辛驳回了对他的指控，称其毫无根据。她称他的被捕是“有针对性的恐吓”，并表示他的案件表明“政府大规模压制新闻自由的程度”。 马辛强调，乌鲁达拥有良好的网络和关键资源。她说，从政府的角度来看，这正是可能使他成为一个不方便且具有潜在危险的声音的原因。 新闻自由监督机构无国界记者组织 (RSF) 的土耳其代表埃罗尔·翁德罗格鲁 (Erol Onderoglu) 表示，乌鲁达山“被受制于当权者的司法机构任意针对”。他补充说，乌鲁达被他描述为“一位以调查公共利益问题而闻名的严肃记者”，他的调查可能激怒了当权者。 乌鲁达本人认为他的被捕是故意阻止他继续工作。他此前曾就他声称公正报道的主题报告过起诉书中的矛盾和关键证人证词中的不一致之处。 “我没有偏离我的新闻工作。我相信司法部门的大多数成员本身也对日益政治化的诉讼感到担忧，”他说。 “我将继续追查真相。我不承认任何指控。” 这位记者还将他的被拘留时期描述为一段矛盾的经历。他说，虽然有机会近距离观察监狱的日常生活和囚犯的精神状态对他个人来说很困难，但同时这对于他作为一名司法记者的工作来说具有重要的新闻意义。 乌鲁达并不是土耳其唯一一位被...

title.en: Taiwan: Trump prods China with offer of direct Taipei talks
title.zh: 台湾：特朗普提议与台北直接对话，以此刺激中国

summary.en: Donald Trump has indicated he would engage in direct talks with Taiwan's president regarding the purchase of US arms. This action would deviate from established diplomatic norms of over four decades and is expected to be perceived as a challenge by China.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾领导人就购买美国武器进行直接对话。此举将打破四十多年的外交惯例，并可能被中国视为一种冒犯。

body.en:
Donald Trump has said he will talk with Taiwan's president about purchasing US arms. The move would break over four decades of protocol and be an affront to China.

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday reiterated his intention to hold direct talks with Taiwan 's President Lai Ching-te over a reported $14 billion (€12 billion) arms deal — the first direct talks between the presidents of both countries in over four decades.

"I'll speak to him. I speak to everybody," said Trump when asked about the situation.

Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Lai would be "happy to discuss these matters with President Trump."

It added that Lai is "committed to maintaining the stable status quo in the Taiwan Strait."

Trump's statement was the second such made since his state visit to China last week.

The US leader previously said he had "a great meeting" with Chinese President Xi Jinping , adding, "We'll work on that… the Taiwan problem."

The US officially shifted Taiwanese diplomatic recognition from Taipei (the Republic of China, or ROC) to Beijing (the People's Republic of China, or PRC) in 1979 as part of its "One China" policy of strategic ambiguity and has not engaged in public presidential communications with Taiwanese leaders since that time.

That same year, the US also established the Taiwan Relations Act, committing itself by law to providing Taiwan with the means to defend itself against regional threats.

Although the US has continued to engage in backchannel talks with Taiwan, public displays of support from Washington are frowned upon by Beijing, which considers the self-governing democracy part of its territory and has threatened to take the island republic by force if necessary.

During Trump's recent state visit, China's Xi made clear that the handling of the Taiwan issue would be key to maintaining stability in US-China relations, warning that missteps could lead to an "extremely dangerous situation."

Trump has suggested US arms sales could be used as a bargaining chip with Beijing on the issue.

A spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry urged Trump to "handle the Taiwan issue with extreme caution and stop sending wrong signals to the separatist forces of Taiwan independence."

Taiwan is heavily reliant on US arms to deter China and is eager to double down on the $11 billion deal approved by the Trump administration in December.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾总统讨论购买美国武器的问题。此举将打破四十多年来的协议，是对中国的侮辱。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三重申，他打算与台湾总统赖清德就一项据报道价值 140 亿美元（120 亿欧元）的军火交易进行直接会谈，这是四十多年来两国总统之间的首次直接会谈。 当被问及情况时，特朗普说：“我会和他说话。我会和每个人说话。” 台湾外交部周四表示，赖清德将“很乐意与特朗普总统讨论这些问题”。 声明补充说，黎智英“致力于维持台湾海峡的稳定现状”。 这是特朗普自上周对中国进行国事访问以来第二次发表此类声明。 这位美国领导人此前曾表示，他与中国国家主席习近平进行了“一次精彩的会面”，并补充道，“我们将致力于解决台湾问题。” 作为其“一个中国”战略模糊政策的一部分，美国于 1979 年正式将与台湾的外交承认从台北（中华民国，简称 ROC）转向北京（中华人民共和国，简称中华人民共和国），并且从那时起就没有与台湾领导人进行公开的总统沟通。 同年，美国还制定了《与台湾关系法》，依法承诺为台湾提供防御地区威胁的手段。 尽管美国继续与台湾进行秘密谈判，但北京方面对华盛顿公开表示支持表示不满，北京认为自治民主是其领土的一部分，并威胁在必要时以武力占领这个岛国。 在特朗普最近的国事访问期间，中国国家主席习近平明确表示，处理台湾问题是维护美中关系稳定的关键，并警告说，失误可能导致“极其危险的局面”。 特朗普表示，美国的军售可以作为在这个问题上与北京讨价还价的筹码。 中国外交部发言人敦促特朗普“高度谨慎处理台湾问题，停止向台独分裂势力发出错误信号”。 台湾严重依赖美国武器来威慑中国，并渴望加倍落实特朗普政府去年 12 月批准的 110 亿美元协议。

title.en: Xi and Putin condemn ‘irresponsible’ US foreign policy at Beijing summit
title.zh: 习近平和普京在北京峰会上谴责美国“不负责任”的外交政策

summary.en: Chinese and Russian leaders, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, met in Beijing and jointly condemned what they termed “irresponsible” US foreign policy, warning of a potential “drift back to the law of the jungle” in international relations.
summary.zh: 中国和俄罗斯领导人习近平和普京在北京峰会上谴责美国“不负责任”的外交政策，并警告国际关系可能“倒退回丛林法则”。

body.en:
Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin issued a joint condemnation of “irresponsible” US foreign policy on Wednesday, warning of “a drift back to the law of the jungle”.

The statement came after the Chinese and Russian leaders held a summit in Beijing that followed a visit to the capital by Donald Trump.

The exchanges between Xi and Putin were notably warm and Wednesday’s summit appeared to be more substantive than Xi’s meetings with the US president.

In their joint statement, Xi and Putin said they looked forward to further bilateral cooperation ranging from artificial intelligence to the protection of rare tigers, leopards and pandas. However, they failed to finalise an agreement over a pipeline that would allow Russia to double its fossil gas exports to China . Industry observers suggested that pricing was the biggest obstacle to a contract being signed.

The spectacle of the leaders of the cold war superpowers – each weakened by conflicts of their own making – flying thousands of miles to sit down with Xi in the Great Hall of the People underlined the Chinese president’s status on the global stage.

Xi and Putin went into their summit with a long record of close cooperation. They had already met more than 40 times, and Xi has described the bilateral relation as “without limits”.

The two leaders scolded the US for undermining global stability, in particular for seeking to develop a “golden dome” missile defence system, and for allowing a nuclear arms treaty to lapse in February.

“The global agenda of peace and development is facing new risks and challenges, with the danger of fragmentation of the international community and a drift back towards the ‘law of the jungle’,” the joint declaration said, according to the Kremlin.

Putin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has brought Russia and China closer together while increasing the Russian leader’s dependence on Beijing for support in the face of isolation by western countries. Reuters cited three European intelligence agencies as saying China had secretly trained about 200 Russian soldiers late last year, some of whom had returned to fight in Ukraine.

Beijing is officially neutral in the conflict but has continued to conduct military exercises with Moscow, and there have been numerous reports of covert Chinese assistance.

Putin’s visit followed a similar protocol to Trump’s. Chinese soldiers stood in position as a military band played the Russian and Chinese national anthems for the leaders in central Beijing. Children waved Russian and Chinese flags and cheered “welcome, welcome!” before the pair entered the hall.

body.zh: 习近平和普京周三联合谴责美国“不负责任”的外交政策，警告美国“回归丛林法则”。 该声明是在唐纳德·特朗普访问北京后，中国和俄罗斯领导人在北京举行峰会之后发表的。 习近平和普京之间的交流尤其热烈，周三的峰会似乎比习近平与美国总统的会晤更具实质性。 习近平和普京在联合声明中表示，期待进一步加强从人工智能到保护珍稀老虎、豹子和大熊猫等领域的双边合作。然而，他们未能敲定一条管道协议，该管道将使俄罗斯对中国的化石天然气出口增加一倍。行业观察家表示，定价是签署合同的最大障碍。 冷战时期的超级大国领导人 — — 每一个都因自己制造的冲突而被削弱 — — 飞越数千英里，在人民大会堂与习近平坐在一起，这一景象突显了中国国家主席在全球舞台上的地位。 习近平和普京在峰会上有着长期的密切合作。他们已经会晤了40多次，习近平形容双边关系“没有极限”。 两位领导人谴责美国破坏全球稳定，特别是寻求发展“金顶”导弹防御系统，并允许核武器条约在二月份失效。 克里姆林宫称，联合声明称，“全球和平与发展议程正面临新的风险和挑战，存在国际社会分裂和倒退到‘丛林法则’的危险。” 普京对乌克兰的全面入侵拉近了俄罗斯和中国的距离，同时也增加了俄罗斯领导人在面对西方国家孤立时对北京支持的依赖。路透社援引三个欧洲情报机构的话说，中国去年底秘密训练了约200名俄罗斯士兵，其中一些人已返回乌克兰参加战斗。 北京在冲突中官方保持中立，但继续与莫斯科进行军事演习，并且有大量关于中国秘密援助的报道。 普京的访问遵循了与特朗普类似的程序。在北京市中心，军乐团为领导人演奏俄罗斯和中国国歌时，中国士兵站在原地。孩子们挥舞着俄罗斯和中国国旗，欢呼着“欢迎，欢迎！”两人进入大厅之前。 习近平和普京的会谈以一次简短的“狭义会议”开始，讨论敏感问题。随后举行了一场有更多代表参加的“宽幅会议”，会议于下午 2 点左右结束……

title.en: Rosenberg: Putin enjoys Xi's Chinese welcome but heads home without pipeline deal
title.zh: 罗森伯格：普京享受习近平的中国式欢迎，但回国时未达成管道协议

summary.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited China, where he was welcomed by President Xi Jinping. Despite a show of unity on the world stage, the visit concluded without a major pipeline deal, indicating limits to the partnership, according to the BBC's Russia Editor.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京访问中国，受到习近平主席的欢迎。据英国广播公司俄罗斯编辑报道，尽管两国在世界舞台上展现了团结，但此次访问并未达成重要的天然气管道协议，这表明两国伙伴关系存在局限。

body.en:
As Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping walked the red carpet towards the Great Hall of the People, a Chinese military band played the romantic Russian classic Moscow Nights.

It was the language of two leaders who like to show they've built a special relationship. They have had plenty of time to do so: they have met more than 40 times over the years.

In their public statements they spoke of "strategic co-operation" between their nations, about "partnership", "mutual respect", "friendship" and "trust."

Together they railed against the "irresponsible" nuclear policy of the United States and condemned Donald Trump's plan for a Golden Dome missile defence shield.

On the eve of the visit the Russian government newspaper had published two big photos on its front page: one of a lonely-looking Trump climbing the steps of Air Force One at the end of his China trip last week; and beside it an old image of Putin and Xi walking together.

The visual messaging was unmistakable: Russia and China are shoulder-to- shoulder on the world stage.

And in the world of geopolitics relationships are rarely based on love and affection. It's often self-interest.

Russia is keen to push ahead with plans for a new pipeline, Power of Siberia 2, and had hoped for progress in Beijing. The pipeline would bring additional volumes of Russian gas from Western Siberia to Northern China via Mongolia and, for Moscow, help make up for the loss of European markets.

Last year Russia and China had signed a memorandum of understanding on the project, but Beijing appears in no rush to do the deal. As well as pricing issues, some commentators believe China wants to avoid over-dependence on Russian fossil fuels.

On Wednesday the Kremlin said Russia and China had reached a "general understanding on the parameters" of the project.

"The positions of Russia and China are not identical. Their interests do not always coincide," the Russian government newspaper had conceded: the same edition that had published the photo of Putin and Xi side-by-side.

"With two countries of this size, both with a great-power psyche, it couldn't be any other way."

It wasn't so long ago that the word "bromance" was being applied to another high-level relationship: this time Putin-Trump, as Russia and America pledged to thaw ties.

After the two presidents met in Alaska last summer Russian officials began referring to "the spirit of Anchorage" and hinting that Moscow and Washington had reached a mutual understanding on how to end the war in Ukraine (on terms acceptable to Moscow).

"The spirit of Beijing exists," Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said on the sidelines of the summit.
body.zh: 当弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平走上红地毯走向人民大会堂时，中国军乐队演奏了浪漫的俄罗斯经典《莫斯科之夜》。 这是两位领导人想要表明他们已经建立了特殊关系的语言。他们有充足的时间这样做：这些年来他们已经会面了 40 多次。 他们在公开声明中谈到了两国之间的“战略合作”、“伙伴关系”、“相互尊重”、“友谊”和“信任”。 他们共同谴责美国“不负责任”的核政策，并谴责唐纳德·特朗普的金顶导弹防御系统计划。 访问前夕，俄罗斯政府报纸在头版刊登了两张大照片：一张是特朗普上周结束中国之行时，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在访问中国期间，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在中国访问结束后，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在访问中国期间，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶。旁边是普京和习近平一起散步的老照片。 视觉信息是明确无误的：俄罗斯和中国在世界舞台上并肩作战。 在地缘政治世界中，关系很少是建立在爱和感情的基础上的。这往往是出于自身利益。 俄罗斯热衷于推进新管道“西伯利亚力量2号”的计划，并希望北京能够取得进展。该管道将​​把更多的俄罗斯天然气从西西伯利亚经蒙古输送到中国北部，对于莫斯科来说，有助于弥补欧洲市场的损失。 去年，俄罗斯和中国就该项目签署了谅解备忘录，但北京方面似乎并不急于达成协议。除了定价问题外，一些评论人士认为，中国希望避免过度依赖俄罗斯化石燃料。 克里姆林宫周三表示，俄罗斯和中国已就该项目的“参数达成总体谅解”。 俄罗斯政府报纸承认：“俄罗斯和中国的立场并不相同。他们的利益并不总是一致的。”该报纸还刊登了普京和习近平并肩的照片。 “对于两个如此规模的国家，都具有大国心态，没有其他办法了。” 不久前，“兄弟情谊”这个词还被应用于另一种高层关系：这次是普京与特朗普，俄罗斯和美国承诺解冻关系。 去年夏天两国总统在阿拉斯加会晤后，俄罗斯官员开始提及“安克雷奇精神”，并暗示莫斯科和华盛顿已就如何结束乌克兰战争达成了共同谅解（以莫斯科可接受的条件）。 “北京精神是存在的，”普京的外交政策助手尤里·乌沙科夫在峰会间隙表示。

reflection.en: The news highlights how even strong international alliances can face limits when national interests diverge. While leaders may project unity, the practicalities of specific deals often reveal underlying priorities. This reminds us that ultimate loyalties shape our actions, and nations, like individuals, often find themselves serving distinct "masters" when...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻揭示了即使是强大的国际联盟，当国家利益出现分歧时，也会面临局限。尽管领导人可能展现团结，但具体交易的实际情况往往会暴露出潜在的优先事项。这提醒我们，最终的忠诚塑造着我们的行动，国家和个人一样，在经济或战略利益面前，常常会发现自己侍奉着不同的“主人”。

verse.textEn: No one can serve two masters... You cannot serve both God and Mammon.
verse.textZh: 一个人不能事奉两个主……你们不能又事奉神，又事奉玛门。

title.zh: 德国当局逮捕两名涉嫌为中国从事高科技间谍活动的人员

summary.en: Two Munich residents have been arrested on suspicion of working for a Chinese intelligence service, seeking to obtain and pass on high-tech information with "military applications."

title.en: Numbers of Tibetan exiles plummet as China tightens grip
title.zh: 随着中国收紧控制，藏族流亡人数锐减

summary.en: Fewer Tibetans are seeking exile, as escaping Beijing-controlled Tibet has become more complicated and dangerous. The drop raises questions about preserving the future of Tibetan culture.
summary.zh: 随着北京对西藏的控制日益收紧，逃离西藏变得更加复杂和危险，寻求流亡的藏族人数量锐减。这一下降引发了人们对保护藏族文化未来的担忧。

body.en:
Fewer Tibetans are seeking exile, as escaping Beijing-controlled Tibet has become more complicated and dangerous. The drop raises questions about preserving the future of Tibetan culture.

For decades, the steady flow of Tibetans escaping across the Himalayas into India and Nepal served as a barometer of conditions inside Tibet.

From the late 1990s through the mid‑2000s, several thousand Tibetans sought exile every year, bringing firsthand accounts of political restrictions, cultural pressures and daily life under Chinese rule. 

But data from the Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamsala, the de facto capital of Tibetans in exile where the 14th Dalai Lama also resides, has revealed a collapse in the number of newly arrived Tibetans

Between 1995 and 1999, more than 12,000 Tibetans successfully sought exile. In the past five years, that number has plummeted to just 81.

With fewer Tibetans able to leave, independent information is becoming scarcer. That has made Beijing's policies, like religious regulation, language reforms, or rural relocation, more opaque to the outside world.

This comes as Beijing is increasingly promoting its own narratives on development and stability in Tibet. 

Lobsang, a middle-aged man who left Tibet in 2010, said the drop in the number of exiles comes as China has tightened its grip.

"Since 2008, the security architecture within Tibet has undergone a total transformation," he told DW.

"What we see now is a high-tech surveillance web where every village, every monastery and every household is monitored. Reaching the border is now nearly impossible for the average Tibetan," he added. 

The data suggests that the steepest drop in exiles began after large-scale protests in 2008 that spread across Tibet ahead of the Beijing Summer Olympics, prompting a heavy security response from Chinese authorities.

In the years that followed, Beijing expanded policing, digital surveillance and border enforcement across the Tibetan Plateau. 

Chinese authorities say their policies in Tibet have improved living standards, built out infrastructure and reduced poverty, leading to fewer people leaving.

The Chinese government has invested heavily in infrastructure , urban development and public services across Tibetan regions. In the eyes of Beijing, the porous border was a liability.

"The young Tibetan population … is increasingly migrating to larger [Chinese] cities and seeking to benefit from the growing Chinese economy," said Atul Kumar, a fellow with the strategic studies program at the Delhi-based Observer Research Foundation (ORF) think tank.

body.zh: 随着逃离北京控制的西藏变得更加复杂和危险，寻求流亡的藏人越来越少。这一下降引发了有关保护西藏文化未来的问题。 几十年来，藏人不断越过喜马拉雅山逃往印度和尼泊尔，成为西藏境内状况的晴雨表。 从 20 世纪 90 年代末到 2000 年代中期，每年都有数千名藏人寻求流亡，带来有关中国统治下的政治限制、文化压力和日常生活的第一手资料。 但位于达兰萨拉（实际上是流亡藏人的首府，也是第十四世达赖喇嘛居住地）的藏人行政中央的数据显示，新抵达的藏人数量锐减 1995年至1999年间，超过12,000名藏人成功寻求流亡。在过去五年里，这个数字已骤降至 81 人。 随着能够离开的藏人越来越少，独立的信息也变得越来越少。这使得北京的宗教管制、语言改革或农村搬迁等政策对外界更加不透明。 在此之际，北京正在越来越多地宣传自己关于西藏发展和稳定的叙述。 2010年离开西藏的中年男子洛桑表示，随着中国加强控制，流亡人数下降。 “自 2008 年以来，西藏的安全架构发生了彻底的转变，”他告诉德国之声。 “我们现在看到的是一个高科技监控网络，每个村庄、每个寺院、每个家庭都受到监控。对于普通藏人来说，到达边境现在几乎是不可能的，”他补充道。 数据显示，2008年北京夏季奥运会之前，西藏各地发生大规模抗议活动，促使中国当局采取了严厉的安全应对措施，之后流亡人数出现了最大幅度的下降。 在接下来的几年里，北京扩大了青藏高原的警务、数字监控和边境执法。 中国当局表示，他们在西藏的政策提高了生活水平，建设了基础设施，减少了贫困，从而减少了离开西藏的人。 中国政府在西藏地区的基础设施、城市发展和公共服务方面投入了大量资金。在北京看来，漏洞百出的边境是一种负担。 位于德里的观察者研究基金会（ORF）智囊团战略研究项目研究员阿图尔·库马尔表示：“年轻的藏族人口......正在越来越多地迁移到[中国]大城市，并寻求从不断增长的中国经济中受益。” 观察家承认社会经济...

Proverbs 28:15 reminds us of the vulnerability of a people under a harsh ruler, likening them to a helpless flock before a predator. In such times, we are called to remember those whose voices are suppressed and whose heritage...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了藏族人民在日益严密的管控下，为保护其文化和自由所面临的严峻挑战。箴言28:15提醒我们，在残暴的统治者之下，人民是多么脆弱，如同无助的羊群面对捕食者。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召去记念那些声音被压制、文化遗产受威胁的人们。
